en: The Commentary on the Meaning of the *Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī*,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master and Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Temple,
in accordance with imperial decree.
Namo bhagavate trailokyaprativiśiṣṭāya buddhāya bhagavate tadyathā.
That which is so called is also said to be "Oṃ," and is further described as "the primordial non-arising of all phenomena" (sarvadharma-anutpāda),
and also as the "Tripiṭaka."

It is also called the Tathāgata’s mark of the invisible crown (*anavalokitamūrdhatā*). *Viśuddha* (purified), *viśodhaya* (purify)! *Sama-sama* (equally, equally), *samantāvabhāsa* (universally illuminating)! *Spharaṇa* (pervading), *sphurita* (radiating) throughout the dense forest of the six realms of existence (*ṣaḍgati*)! *Svabhāva-viśuddhe* (O you whose intrinsic nature is pure)! *Abhiṣiñca mām* (consecrate me)! *Jaya* (Be Victorious)! *Jaya* (Be Victorious)! *Jaya* (Be Victorious)! *Jaya* (Be Victorious
The sublime instruction of the *Amṛtapiśācī*, the nectar-consecration, also known as the consecration of the deathless word (*amṛtapada*).
*Lu* refers to the dharmakāya liberation; *āhara āhara* means "please accept [me]."
Please deign to grant me your acceptance and protection.

Also known as "The Universal Dispeller of All Suffering and Affliction," *āyurvardhanī* (the sustainer of life), *śodhaya śodhaya* (purify, purify), *viśuddha-viśuddha-gaganaviśuddhe* (O you who are pure like the utterly pure sky), *uṣṇīṣavijayā-vijayini* (O Victorious One, the Victory of the Uṣṇīṣa), "The Most Pure Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa," *svāhā*, *sarasvatī* (O Sarasvatī), *prabodhaya sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhānādhiṣṭhite* (awaken, O you who are empowered by the empowerment of all Tathāgatas), *mahāmudre* (O Great Seal).
Regarding the mudrās:
to explain them in detail,
there are the body mudrā, the speech mudrā, and the mind mudrā.
The Vajra Seal.

As stated in the *Tattvasaṃgraha-prajñāpāramitā*: "Vajrakāyasamhatānāṃ viśuddhe" (O you who are the purification of the vajra-bodies joined together); "sarvavaraṇapāpanudye pariviśuddhe" (O you who remove all obscurations and sins, O completely purified one). All is pure.
All obstacles—namely, the obstacle of karma (*karmāvaraṇa*), the obstacle of retribution (*vipākāvaraṇa*), and the obstacle of afflictions (*kleśāvaraṇa*)—are all rendered pure.

*Pratinihata* (eradicated). *Āyuḥ-pravardhana* (increasing lifespan) is all rendered pure. *Samayādhiṣṭhehi* (be empowered by the pledge). *Maṇi maṇi mahāmaṇi* (jewel, jewel, great jewel), the Worldly Jewel and the Dharma Jewel.

That which is called the three kinds of provisions—merit, wisdom, and the *tathatā-pada* (the state of suchness)—is the entry into the *bhūta-koṭi* (the limit of reality), pervading and pure throughout the *tathatā-bhūtakoṭi*. It is the manifestation of the purity of wisdom; it is the most excellent, the most excellent: *jaya jaya*.
*Vijaya vijaya maṃ svāhā.* Through the two gates of compassion and wisdom, *samāra samāra*, may the characteristics of calm abiding (*śamatha*) and special insight (*vipaśyanā*) be established.
*Sarvabuddhādhiṣṭhita śuddhe praveśa bodhicitta svāhā.* May all Buddhas grant their empowerment; O pure one, enter into the mind of awakening.
Firm as a vajra—*vajra-dṛḍha*. Realize the Vajragarbha—*vajragarbha-abhisambudhya*.
May it be accomplished as a vajra—*vajra-bhava*. *Tummo* (or *tuma*).
Whether reciting for oneself or for another, call out their name: *śrīṃ sarvasattvānāṃ jñānakāyasya viśuddhe*.
Sarvasattvadehaśuddhe svāhā | Sarvagatipariśuddhe svāhā | Sarvatathāgatasamayasiddhiṣṭite svāhā | Mudre mudre vidyā | Svāhā.
It also causes awakening to that which is capable of awakening.

It causes awakening to the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) of the Universal Purity of the Successive Stages of Awakening, empowered by the spiritual power of all Tathāgatas (*sarvatathāgatādhiṣṭhāna-adhiṣṭhitā*). *Sarva-tathāgata-adhiṣṭhāna-adhiṣṭhitā mahāmudrā*.
Regarding what is called the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā): after entering the Vairocana maṇḍala and receiving empowerment,
the preceptor receives the samādhi of the yoga of the tutelary deity.
Through the wisdom of contemplation and a single thought of pure mind,
the practitioner who accords with yoga becomes identical in heart-mind with the specific honored deity and all bodhisattvas, such as Vairocana;
thus they are able to manifest the signs of entering and accomplishing the Way.
"May one swiftly realize the wisdom of sarvajñā; svāhā" has the meaning of *nirvāṇa*, namely the four types of *nirvāṇa*:
first, *prakṛti-viśuddhi-nirvāṇa* (nirvāṇa of intrinsic purity).
Second, nirvana with remainder;
third, nirvana without remainder;
fourth, non-abiding nirvana.
As translated above, the Chinese and Sanskrit terms are set in opposition;
this is a commentary on the *Prasphuṭapadā*.
This book has been completed. It was transcribed by the Acharya Enkaku Jisen of Kegotoku-in in Tosotsu Valley and proofread by him himself. Recorded by Ryūkan.
